source_text: Sed videamus et cetera. Sed non sicut delictum ita gratia; si enim in unius delicto multi mortui sunt, multo magis gratia Dei et donum in gratia unius hominis Iesu Christi in plures abundavit [n330] . Superari dicit malum delicti copia gratiae et eorum qui salvantur numerum illis, quos praevaricatione perisse asserit, anteponit.
pass_a_gloss: But let us see also the rest. But not as the offense so grace; for if in the offense of one many died, much more the grace of God and the gift in the grace of one human being Jesus Christ abounded unto more. He says that the evil of the offense is surpassed by a plenty of grace and he sets the number of those who are saved before those whom he asserts have perished by transgression.

lemmas.lexica: LS praevaricatio; Blaise Adam's transgression as example
LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS donum; Blaise grace-gift vs inherited sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: But let us examine the rest. ‘But grace is not like the offense. For if in one man’s offense many died, much more did God’s grace and the gift in the grace of the one man Jesus Christ abound to more people’ (Romans 5:15). He says that the evil of the offense is surpassed by the abundance of grace, and ranks the number of those saved above those whom he declares to have perished through transgression.

choices.why: Adam's act of crossing the command; Julian's example of sin, not a transmitted nature.
Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
